text:
Priya (PM): Quick sync on API Keys UX update. We're trying an inline 'row expansion' pattern for quick rotates and disables. Figma: https://figma.com/s/row-expand-keys
Carlos (eng): Sounds useful. Quick Q: will inline rotate generate a new secret in-place or open the modal?
Tess (design): In-place. Small panel reveals 'rotate' which creates a new secret and starts a 15-30min overlap window. We show a tiny timer and an "Undo" while overlap is active.
Rae (a11y): Accessibility notes: when expanding, focus must jump into the panel and the screen reader should get an aria-live announcement: "Key details opened for <name>". Also any newly revealed secret must be programmatically focusable and have proper labels.
Priya (PM): Create flow unchanged: modal with a single-show secret. Copy: "Secret shown once — download now or copy to your vault." Primary CTA: "Download secret".
Carlos (eng): Edge: revoke vs disable. I prefer two-step: inline 'Disable' which blocks new tokens but doesn't affect current sessions; full 'Revoke' in drawer that invalidates existing tokens. Safer for customers.
Tess (design): Agree. Use amber for inline Disable, reserve red for Revoke confirm. In-line we display a small 'Admin' tag for keys with wide scopes.
Rae (a11y): Ensure Disable/Revoke buttons are distinguishable via more than color (icons and text). Provide clear aria-describedby explaining the effect of each action.
Priya (PM): Empty state copy: "No API keys yet. Create one to start integrating Redwood. Tip: use a dev (read-only) key for testing." Include a one-line quickstart code snippet and set focus on the primary CTA.
release-bot: release:preview deployed -> https://preview.redwood.ai/keys-row
Carlos (eng): We'll add telemetry: show last-used timestamp and masked top IPs in the expansion to help decide whether to revoke.
Priya (PM): Great. I'll update the mocks with these a11y and copy changes and post a new link tomorrow. Thanks! :tada:
